columnPool.label: Route: Fife Circle
columnPool.display: Is part of the Fife Circle route
columnPool.hint: The commuter route north of Edinburgh looping through Fife via Dunfermline, Cowdenbeath, Kirkcaldy and Glenrothes, crossing the Forth Bridge - two originally separate lines joined into one circuit in 1989.

columnPool.label: Route: Shotts Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Shotts Line route
columnPool.hint: The slower of the two Edinburgh-Glasgow routes, running via Shotts and West Calder rather than the faster main line via Falkirk - about twice the journey time of the direct service.

columnPool.label: Route: Borders Railway
columnPool.display: Is part of the Borders Railway route
columnPool.hint: The reopened line south from Edinburgh through Newtongrange and Galashiels to Tweedbank - Britain's longest new domestic railway in over a century when it opened in 2015, on the former Waverley Route.

columnPool.label: Route: North Berwick Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the North Berwick Line route
columnPool.hint: The branch east from Edinburgh along the East Lothian coast via Prestonpans and Drem to the seaside town of North Berwick.

columnPool.label: Route: Argyle Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Argyle Line route
columnPool.hint: This tag actually covers the Edinburgh-Bathgate corridor (Armadale, Bathgate, Edinburgh Park, Livingston North) - the real Argyle Line is a different, unrelated route: Glasgow's underground low-level crosstown line linking Dalmuir/Milngavie through Glasgow Central Low Level to Motherwell, Lanark and Coatbridge.

columnPool.label: Route: North Clyde Electrics
columnPool.display: Is part of the North Clyde Electrics route
columnPool.hint: The wider North Clyde suburban network radiating from Glasgow Queen Street, which also extends east to Edinburgh via the Bathgate branch through Armadale, Livingston North and Edinburgh Park.

columnPool.label: Route: Edinburgh-Glasgow Main Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Edinburgh-Glasgow Main Line route
columnPool.hint: The fast, direct route between the two cities via Falkirk High and Linlithgow - the premier Edinburgh-Glasgow service, quicker than the alternative via Shotts.
